content_html:
After touring the impressive Peruvian landscapes, there is nothing better than soaking in natural hot springs to relax your muscles and revitalize your body. Peru, with its intense geothermal activity, offers various options for thermal baths, ideal for those seeking rest after long walks or explorations in nature. Here we present some of the best hot springs in the country.

1. Lares Hot Springs (Cusco)

Located in the Lares Valley, about 3 hours from Cusco, these hot springs are perfect for those who have done the trek from Lares to Machu Picchu or some walk in the area.

Features:

  • It has several swimming pools with temperatures ranging between 36°C and 44°C.
  • Its waters contain minerals beneficial for the skin and muscles.
  • Surrounded by mountains and nature, they offer an atmosphere of total tranquility.

Ideal for:
Relax after a demanding hike or a visit to Machu Picchu.

2. Cocalmayo Hot Springs (Santa Teresa, Cusco)

After a long walk through the Inca Trail or Salkantay, these hot springs are the best rest before reaching Machu Picchu. Located in Saint Teresa, near Hidroeléctrica, are a mandatory stop for adventurers.

Features:

  • They are of the most crystalline hot springs in Peru.
  • They have temperatures between 38°C and 44°C.
  • Surrounded by tropical vegetation and mountains, they offer a paradisiacal atmosphere.

Ideal for:
Travelers traveling the alternative route to Machu Picchu and they are looking for relaxation before the big visit.

3. Churín Hot Springs (Lima)

If you are looking for a thermal destination near Lima, Churín is the best option. Just 4 hours from the capital, it is famous for its various hot springs with healing properties.

Features:

  • The best known are Mamahuarmi, Tingo and Fierro, each one with different temperatures and minerals.
  • Its waters are rich in iron, lithium and sulfur, ideal for relieving muscle pain and skin problems.
  • It also has spa services and natural massages with volcanic mud.

Ideal for:
A weekend getaway from Lima or a stop after an adventure in the Nor Yauyos-Cochas Reserve.

4. Hot Springs of Baños del Inca (Cajamarca)

This site is historical, since it was a resting place for the Inca Atahualpa. It is located just 10 minutes from the city of Cajamarca and is one of the best-known thermal complexes in the country.

Features:

  • Its waters range between 35°C and 70°C, ideal for therapeutic baths.
  • It offers private pools and steam rooms.
  • Water has healing properties for the nervous and circulatory system.

Ideal for:
Relax after exploring the history of Cajamarca, like the Cuarto del Rescate or the Windows of Otuzco.

5. Aguas Calientes Hot Springs (Machu Picchu)

If after exploring the wonder of Machu Picchu You need a break, these hot springs are the perfect option. They are located in the town of Hot Waters, a few minutes walk from the center.

Features:

  • Several pools with temperatures between 38°C and 46°C.
  • Surrounded by mountains and jungle vegetation.
  • An excellent relaxation point after a day of exploration in Machu Picchu.

Ideal for:
Relax after an intense day touring the Inca citadel.

Tips to Enjoy the Hot Springs to the Fullest

He wears a bathing suit and sandals, since in some places it is mandatory.
Hydrate well before and after bathing, since hot water can cause dehydration.
Do not stay in the water for more than 20-30 minutes at a time., to avoid dizziness.
Visit during less busy times, such as early in the morning or at night, for greater peace of mind.
